evidence: Levi–Bini p. 19: corōna, the frame of a picture
terms.comment: Levi and Bini’s word for a picture’s frame. Classically corōna is a garland or wreath, anything that rings something round (Lewis & Short); the picture frame is the modern sense. Where a garland might be understood, say corōna tabulae or corōna pictūrae.
The border of anything, of a cup, a gem, or a page; for the frame round a picture the use is ours.

phrases.latin: Pictūram tuam corōnā cingāmus et in pariete suspendāmus.
phrases.english: Let’s put your picture in a frame and hang it on the wall.

phrases.latin: Corōna pictūrae oblīqua est: rēctam fac.
phrases.english: The picture frame is crooked: straighten it.

sources: Lewis & Short: corona · Lewis & Short: margo
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 19, s.v. cornice.
